sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Strategic Context**: Aurangzeb dispatched **Mirza Raja Jai Singh** to the Deccan in 1665 to neutralize Shivaji after the failure of Shaista Khan.
• **The Treaty Mechanism**: Signed on **June 11, 1665**, it forced Shivaji to surrender 23 of his 35 forts to the Mughals.
• **Geopolitical Objective**: The treaty aimed to isolate the **Bijapur Sultanate** by using Maratha military prowess as a proxy force for the Mughals.
• **Key Metric**: Shivaji was left with only 12 forts and an annual revenue of 1 lakh huns, effectively reducing his sovereign status to a Mughal vassal.

items.definition: The Rajput general of Aurangzeb who successfully negotiated the treaty; he represented the Mughal 'Rajput-Mughal' alliance model.
Shivaji's son, Sambhaji, was granted a Mansab of 5,000, integrating the Maratha leadership into the Mughal hierarchy.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Strategic Proxy**: Using Maratha cavalry to weaken Bijapur, saving Mughal resources.
• **Agra Visit**: The treaty paved the way for Shivaji's visit to the Mughal court in 1666, which ultimately led to his escape.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: The treaty was inherently unstable due to mutual distrust and the clash of imperial vs. regional aspirations.
• **Solutions**: Shivaji's subsequent 'Coronation' (1674) marked the formal rejection of the vassal status established by the treaty.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-J-S' (Purandar, Jai Singh, Shivaji).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Purandar (1665) was the bridge between Jai Singh (Mughal) and Shivaji (Maratha).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 1665 Treaty of Purandar with the 1776 Treaty of Purandar (Anglo-Maratha War). Always check the century.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Strategic Realism' to describe Shivaji's decision to sign the treaty, highlighting his pragmatism over idealism.

keyTakeaways: The Treaty of Purandar was a tactical retreat for Shivaji to preserve his core power base.
It highlights Aurangzeb's reliance on Rajput generals to manage Deccan affairs.
The failure of the treaty led to the intensification of the Mughal-Maratha conflict, eventually draining the Mughal treasury.
